hero.body: A systemic approach to understanding complex adaptive systems — from human health and cognition to civilizational dynamics. AI-integrated simulation and research tools for every domain.

mission.heading: Beyond Reductionism
mission.body: ISRD moves from traditional reductionist systems analysis to Systemic Engineering — where users (writers, scientists, policy makers) use a shared toolkit to build and publish their own complex system simulators. Every gauge is a node in a directed feedback graph. Every intervention propagates.

about.heading: Independent Systems Research and Development
about.intro: ISRD is the independent research practice of Kurt Rowley — a non-linear, holistic approach to understanding and designing complex systems, published as articles, research notes, courses, and interactive simulations.
about.body: I'm not affiliated with any institution, company, or lab — ISRD is a personal research identity, not an organization. I build simulations to make feedback loops, attractor basins, and bifurcations tangible across domains from post-viral illness to civilizational dynamics to the craft of writing, and I'm open to collaborating with other researchers or organizations on specific projects where the fit is right.

principles.title: Systemic Synthesis Priority
principles.desc: Gauges are not independent variables — they are nodes in a directed graph with edges representing feedback weights.

principles.title: Modular Architecture
principles.desc: Every simulation is pluggable. New models are created by dropping in a new configuration for the shared toolkit.

principles.title: AI Integration Hooks
principles.desc: Components expose hooks that allow AI services to ingest simulation state and suggest systemic adjustments.

principles.title: Design as Evidence
principles.desc: Every project runs the same cycle: map the system, form a testable hypothesis, build an intervention, and fold what happens back into the model. The working system is both the output and the evidence — if the model is wrong, the system built on it fails visibly, and that failure is itself the finding.

about.people_note: ISRD is a solo research practice. All of the writing, research, and simulations here are authored and built by one person, working openly and hoping the work itself is worth reading regardless of institutional affiliation.

people.name: Kurt Rowley
people.title: Independent Researcher
people.bio: Systems thinker, writer, and simulation architect. Kurt works independently to develop a rigorous, non-linear methodology for understanding complex adaptive systems — from post-viral illness to civilisational dynamics to the craft of writing. His work draws on general systems theory, complexity science, cybernetics, and AI-integrated modelling.
